samples.summary: `duplicateTab` copies the worksheet verbatim, so the copy's charts (and its `pivotTable`) still carry `sourceTabId` pointing at the ORIGINAL tab. `chart-utils.ts` resolves chart data with `root.sheets[chart.sourceTabId]`, so every chart on the duplicated tab renders the source tab's numbers, not the copy's — and a duplicated pivot output tab silently becomes a second dependent that makes the new `resolveDelete` refuse to delete the source tab, naming a tab the user never configured.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/chart-utils.ts:116 `const sourceSheet = root.sheets[chart.sourceTabId];` (same at :188 and :281), and packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/pivot/use-pivot-table.ts:135 `const sourceWs = root.sheets[definition.sourceTabId];`. The new duplicate writes `const copy: Worksheet = { ...worksheet, comments: {} }` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/tab-ops.ts, duplicateTab) — chart ids and `sourceTabId`/`pivotTable.sourceTabId` are not remapped to the new tab id. Fix belongs in `duplicateTab`.

samples.summary: `copyThread` detaches the anchor with the generic `detachYorkieValue`, but a docs-range anchor's `posRange` is explicitly documented as a value that does not survive a generic detach. `GET /comments` on a `doc` document therefore returns a `posRange` made of Yorkie CRDT metadata instead of a usable `TreePosStructRange`, so an API consumer cannot resolve or round-trip a docs thread anchor.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/comments/yorkie-comment-store.ts:81-88 states the invariant: "`posRange` is deliberately left as-is. Stored as a Yorkie array, its `toJSON()` returns a string-escaped serialization that does not round-trip through `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))`" — and this branch's own `yorkie-json.ts:13-20` warns that `detachYorkieValue` branches on `Array.isArray`, which is false for a Yorkie array proxy, so it returns `{createdAt, movedAt}` metadata. `copyThread` uses exactly that helper on `t.anchor`, and the comments controller's `list`/`setResolved`/`reply` return its output for `doc` documents.

samples.summary: The shared comments UI gains its first RUNTIME dependency on `@wafflebase/sheets`. `types/comments.ts` imported it type-only (erased at build); `mentions.ts` and `notify.ts` now import values (`serializeMention`, `planCommentNotifications`) from the sheets root index. Those two modules are imported by `CommentBody.tsx`, `CommentSidePanel.tsx`, `OrphanedCard.tsx` and `CommentComposer.tsx`, which the docs editor and the PDF viewer both mount — so the sheets package now enters chunks that previously had no sheets code at all, which is what the per-chunk bundle budget measures.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/types/comments.ts:2 uses `import type { ... } from '@wafflebase/sheets'` (erased); packages/frontend/src/components/comments/mentions.ts:13 is a value import. Consumers outside the sheets app: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/comments/yorkie-comment-store.ts and packages/frontend/src/app/files/comments/pdf-comment-store.ts, via components/comments/components/CommentBody.tsx:3 and CommentSidePanel.tsx:8.

samples.summary: The new author-only rule on comment edit/delete has a reachable server-side way around it, added in the same change: `DELETE /documents/:documentId/tabs/:tabId` deletes the whole worksheet, and with it every comment thread on that tab, with no author check at all. A workspace-scoped API key that is refused `DELETE .../comments/:threadId` for someone else's thread can delete the tab instead. The editor has the same property, so this may be intended — but the comments controller's docblock justifies the check specifically by "these routes are reachable with a workspace-scoped API key", and this route is too.
samples.evidence: `applyDelete` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/tab-ops.ts) does `delete root.sheets[tabId]`, which removes `sheets[tabId].comments` wholesale; `ApiV1TabsController.remove` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/tabs.controller.ts:157) calls it after only `assertSheetDocument`, never `assertCommentAuthor`.

verdict.reason: Every claimed location checks out. `duplicateTab` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/tab-ops.ts:167) writes `{ ...worksheet, comments: {} }`, scrubbing only comments; the `Worksheet` type (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-document.ts:88-99) carries `charts` (each with `sourceTabId`, line 20) and `pivotTable` (sourceTabId at packages/sheets/src/model/core/types.ts:310), so both are copied verbatim with ids pointing at the original tab. The controller path (packages/backend/src/api/v1/tabs.controller.ts:247-270) unwraps the entire source worksheet and passes it through with no remapping and no rejection other than "has no worksheet", and it also copies `meta.kind` (tab-ops.ts:162), so a pivot output tab can be duplicated. The consumers cited resolve data strictly by `sourceTabId`: chart-utils.ts:116, :188, :281 and pivot/use-pivot-table.ts:135 — so the copy's charts render the original tab's numbers and never track edits made on the copy. The dependent consequence is also real: tab-ops.ts:84-92 (`resolveDelete`) and the frontend equivalent at documents/document-detail.tsx:512-537 both scan all tabs' `pivotTable.sourceTabId`, so a duplicated pivot tab becomes an extra dependent that blocks/prompts on deleting the source tab. No guard elsewhere prevents this (tab-ops.spec.ts:178-213 shows only name/order/cells/comments are handled). This is a contract/invariant break observed at call sites outside the diff, which is in the blast-radius lane; severity major stands.

Stored as a Yorkie array, its `toJSON()` returns a string-escaped serialization that does not round-trip through `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))`" — and this branch's own `yorkie-json.ts:13-20` warns that `detachYorkieValue` branches on `Array.isArray`, which is false for a Yorkie array proxy, so it returns `{createdAt, movedAt}` metadata. `copyThread` uses exactly that helper on `t.anchor`, and the comments controller's `list`/`setResolved`/`reply` return its output for `doc` documents.

verdict.reason: Every element checks out in the repo. `copyThread` does route the anchor through the generic walker (comment-ops.ts:99). `detachYorkieValue` branches on `Array.isArray` (yorkie-json.ts:172) which the branch's own doc comment (yorkie-json.ts:13-20), its spec (yorkie-json.spec.ts:155-162) and an archived lessons file (20260827-v1-worksheet-review-fix-lessons.md:13-23) all state is false for a Yorkie array proxy, yielding `{createdAt, movedAt}` metadata. `DocsRangeAnchor.posRange` is a tuple (types/comments.ts:28-33) written straight into the CRDT as a Yorkie array (yorkie-comment-store.ts:164-187), and the docs store documents the invariant that it must not be generically detached (yorkie-comment-store.ts:81-88). The read path is reachable with a live proxy: comments.controller.ts:250-257 calls listThreads(doc.getRoot().comments) and yorkie.service.ts:36-57 supplies a real yorkie.Document; mutateThread (comments.controller.ts:588-602) returns copyThread output for reply/setResolved as well. The POST refusal at comments.controller.ts:276-289 blocks only creation, not listing/replying/resolving, so nothing guards the read. Real, reachable, and a violated cross-module invariant — in-lane and blocking.
